arxiv-2312-01579.title: Enhanced Persistent Orientation of Asymmetric-Top Molecules Induced by Cross-Polarized Terahertz Pulses
arxiv-2312-01579.creator: Long Xu, Ilia Tutunnikov, Yehiam Prior, Ilya Sh. Averbukh
arxiv-2312-01579.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Long Xu, Ilia Tutunnikov, Yehiam Prior, Ilya Sh. Averbukh. We investigate the persistent orientation of asymmetric-top molecules induced by time-delayed THz pulses that are either collinearly or cross polarized. Our theoretical and numerical results demonstrate that the orthogonal configuration outperforms the collinear one, and a significant degree of persistent orientation - approximately 10% at 5 K and nearly 3% at room temperature - may be achieved through parameter optimization.

arxiv-2402-08356.title: Azimuthal metallicity variations, spiral structure, and the failure of radial actions based on assuming axisymmetry Azimuthal metallicity variations, spiral structure, and the failure of radial actions based on assuming axisymmetry – Data Availability —-
arxiv-2402-08356.creator: Victor P. Debattista, Tigran Khachaturyants, João A. S. Amarante, Christopher Carr, Leandro Beraldo e Silva, Chervin F. P. Laporte
arxiv-2402-08356.description: Abstract We study azimuthal variations in the mean stellar metallicity, ⟨ [ Fe / H ] ⟩ \left<{\mbox{$\rm[Fe/H]$}}\right> , in a self-consistent, isolated simulation in which all stars form out of gas. We find ⟨ [ Fe / H ] ⟩ \left<{\mbox{$\rm[Fe/H]$}}\right> variations comparable to those observed in the Milky Way and which are coincident with the spiral density waves.

arxiv-2406-07450.title: Benchmarking Vision-Language Contrastive Methods for Medical Representation Learning
arxiv-2406-07450.creator: Shuvendu Roy Yasaman Parhizkar Franklin Ogidi Vahid Reza Khazaie, Michael Colacci Ali Etemad Elham Dolatabadi Arash Afkanpour
arxiv-2406-07450.description: Abstract We perform a comprehensive benchmarking of contrastive frameworks for learning multimodal representations in the medical domain. Through this study, we aim to answer the following research questions: (i) How transferable are general-domain representations to the medical domain? (ii) Is multimodal contrastive training sufficient, or does it benefit from unimodal training as well?

arxiv-2507-20329.title: Clustering data with values missing at random using scale mixtures of multivariate skew-normal distributions
arxiv-2507-20329.creator: Pillay J, Tortora C, Punzo A, Bekker A
arxiv-2507-20329.description: Abstract Handling missing data is a major challenge in model-based clustering, especially when the data exhibit skewness and heavy tails. We address this by extending the finite mixture of scale mixtures of multivariate skew-normal (FMSMSN) family to accommodate incomplete data under a missing at random (MAR) mechanism.

arxiv-2510-20383.title: Hierarchical Time Series Forecasting with Robust Reconciliation
arxiv-2510-20383.creator: Shuhei Aikawa, Aru Suzuki, Kei Yoshitake, Kanata Teshigawara, Akira Iwabuchi, Ken Kobayashi, Kazuhide Nakata
arxiv-2510-20383.description: Abstract This paper focuses on forecasting hierarchical time-series data, where each higher-level observation equals the sum of its corresponding lower-level time series. In such contexts, the forecast values should be coherent, meaning that the forecast value of each parent series exactly matches the sum of the forecast values of its child series.

arxiv-2602-10867.title: Deep Learning of Compositional Targets with Hierarchical Spectral Methods
arxiv-2602-10867.creator: Hugo Tabanelli, Yatin Dandi, Luca Pesce, Florent Krzakala
arxiv-2602-10867.description: Abstract Why depth yields a genuine computational advantage over shallow methods remains a central open question in learning theory. We study this question in a controlled high-dimensional Gaussian setting, focusing on compositional target functions. We analyze their learnability using an explicit three-layer fitting model trained via layer-wise spectral estimators.

pmc-11352326.creator: Danny Zeevi, Adi Ben Yehuda, Dafna Nathan, David Zangen, Leonid Kruglyak

pmc-13547218.title: CDK1-mediated phosphorylation of EPLIN is crucial for mitotic spindle positioning
pmc-13547218.creator: Jia-Rong Fan, Yun Hsieh, Chien-Chen Lai, Hong-Chen Chen
pmc-13547218.description: Correct anchoring of the mitotic spindle to the cell cortex is essential for proper cell division. However, how the architecture of the cell cortex is coordinately remodeled during mitotic progression remains poorly understood. Here, we show that depletion of EPLIN (an actin-bundling protein) causes spindle deviation and an arrest in metaphase, accompanied with abnormal cortical actin accumulation and blebbing.
